items.title: Every cohomology class on a ringed site is killed on a covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section on cohomology of ringed sites
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a sheaf F of O-modules on a ringed site, an object U, an integer n > 0 and a cohomology class xi in H^n(U, F), some covering {U_i -> U} of the site restricts xi to zero on every U_i (statement lines 716-721). The point that cannot be done by pure formalism is the passage from the class to a representative and from the representative to local primitives: the injective resolution must be used in two ways at once, first to present H^n(U, F) as a quotient of sections of I^n(U) and then, using exactness of the resolution in degree n, to know that the image sheaf of the differential equals the kernel sheaf, which is exactly what produces a covering over which the representative is a coboundary (proof lines 725-741). The class is then killed because restriction of a cohomology class is represented by the restricted section. The claim is H2: short, no citation, but with a genuine two-step use of the resolution.
